prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep a single-part B001 prize to Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. The merit case is unchanged by the unanimous opening: proglucagon processing, the active truncated GLP-1(7-36) amide, human incretin physiology and the receptor pathway are replicated over decades, and large independent outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease confirm that the biology translates. The work is mature, not premature. The chair asks whether the citation should be physiology-led or drug-development-led. I choose physiology-led because the discovery step is what three places can credit cleanly, and the citation can still name the therapeutic consequence. I prefer one achievement to a two-part prize: a second part would take places from a trio whose three roles (human physiology, receptor biology and translation, identification of the active peptide) are each needed, and no second candidate has a clean enough credit to justify the dilution.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakness and round 2 has not removed it. Knudsen's acylation and half-life engineering is what turned a peptide with a half-life of minutes into a once-weekly medicine, so a physiology-only citation can be read as honouring the hormone and not the drug. Mojsov's priority relative to Habener's group is, as the chair notes, resting on members' general knowledge and not on documents we can cite; I cannot settle it either. My position is that if it cannot be defended from cited records, the citation should be worded around the identification and synthesis of the active peptide as a contribution and should not assert exclusive priority. If a majority judges the drug arm to be the core achievement, the right change is Holst, Drucker and Knudsen, replacing Mojsov, and I would accept that over a configuration that names someone whose role the committee cannot defend. The cap forces an exclusion in either direction, and obviousness of the choice is not a reason to skip that scrutiny.

responses.point: The chair asks whether the committee can state from citable documents how priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide divides between Mojsov and Habener's group, and whether failing that changes whether Mojsov is named. He also rejects age alone as a reason to place B008 ahead of clinically active candidates.
responses.response: I cannot answer the priority question from the supplied files, and I do not think anyone at the table can without relying on memory, so I would not let the committee pretend otherwise. What I can do is separate the claims. Holst's human physiology and Drucker's receptor biology stand independent of the Mojsov question. Mojsov's inclusion rests on the identification and synthesis of the active form, which I treat as a distinct and real contribution, but one where I would want the citation worded as a contribution and not as sole priority. If the record proved ambiguous enough to make her naming indefensible, Knudsen is the replacement I would reach for, which makes the drug-arm question and the priority question one decision. On B008 I agree with you and withdraw the weight I gave to age in round 1: Miller and Cooper are foundational, but age is a tie-breaker between equally strong cases and should not lift a purely conceptual prize above B001 this year.

responses.point: Sandberg argues that B010 is mature and cleanly attributed but sits closer to clinical translation than discovery of new biology, that it overlaps with IL-6 (B002), and that he would keep B010 as a later-year candidate behind B051 and B017.
responses.response: The IL-6 overlap is a fair challenge, and I will not claim B010 as the committee's rule for the whole cytokine class. I still disagree that proof that a known cytokine is a therapeutic target is not discovery. The hypothesis that blocking TNF would break the inflammatory cascade in rheumatoid arthritis was tested in patients against the expectation of many, and it opened a class used across arthritis, bowel disease and psoriasis. That is a conceptual step as well as a clinical trial. I accept, though, that your point on discovery weight keeps B010 behind B001, and it is why I hold B010 as an alternative rather than as a second part. Where I side with you is B051: Walter and Mori are a clean pair of mechanistic discovery, but Perlmann's point that PERK and the integrated stress response are left out makes the citation contestable, and I would not place it above B010 or B017.

responses.point: Perlmann reads B017 as lacking a single clean discovery because Eshhar and other early receptor designers are outside the credit and Rosenberg's contribution is adoptive cell transfer, and he keeps it only as a first alternative.
responses.response: I agree with the structure of your objection and it has moved me on B017. Rosenberg, June and Sadelain describe a lineage rather than one discovery, and a citation drawn tightly enough to be accurate would have to leave out either Rosenberg's adoptive transfer or the first chimeric receptor concept. That is a harder attribution problem than the one in B001, where the three credited roles map onto distinct steps. I therefore treat B017 as my second alternative and B010 as my first, because its credit to Feldmann and Maini is cleaner. If B001 stalled, I would want the committee to agree its rule for B017 first: either honour the clinical engineering of CARs by June and Sadelain, or keep the lineage whole and defer the candidate.

responses.point: El-Manira names Holst, Drucker and Knudsen as the fallback if Mojsov's priority is judged too unclear, and ranks optogenetics (B012) second while acknowledging that six credited names cannot be reduced to three without excluding deserving people.
responses.response: Your fallback is the most useful concrete answer to the chair's question, and I support it as the contingency. The discovery side then loses its peptide-identification role, so the citation would need to change to cover physiology, receptor biology and long-acting analogue development, which is a different and defensible prize, not a swap of names. I would have the committee vote on whether the priority record is adequate before deciding between the two sets. On B012 I stay where I was: I accept it is Nobel-scale, but a tool prize with six strong claimants and no agreed rule for the cut is a worse fit for this year than the incretin configuration. I would not support a two-part prize that gave B012 only one or two of three places.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active peptide, relative to Habener's group, can be established from documents the committee can cite. I rely on general knowledge and the committee has not checked supplied records.
Whether the committee regards the drug-development arm (Knudsen) as the core of the achievement; if so the trio should change and the physiology-led citation would be the wrong one.
For B010, whether antibody engineers and TNF cloners fall outside the core credit and how the committee treats the parallel IL-6 success (B002).
For B017, whether Rosenberg's adoptive transfer and Eshhar's early receptor concept can be placed inside or outside the credited set on a stated principle.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for the preferred configuration. I have subject expertise in TNF blockade (B010), which is an alternative and not in my preferred configuration, but no documented personal or institutional connection to Feldmann or Maini. My recorded co-authors (Kuchroo, Sonesson) and my Bergen affiliation do not connect me to any credited person on a shortlisted ballot, and I do not infer ties from shared institutions. No new disclosure arose in round 2.
